newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Syria says Mideast peace process dying.
newsitem.headline: Syria says Mideast peace process dying.

text.p: Syria said on Friday that the Israeli-Palestinian crisis showed the Middle East peace process was dying and accused Israel of trying to destroy it.

"What happens now ... must be a warning for all of us that the peace process ... is dying, the peace process might be buried," Syrian Foreign Minister Farouk al-Shara told a meeting of the U.N. Security Council.
Syria is a key player in wider Middle East peace efforts and has sought the return of the Golan, land occupied by Israel since the Arab-Israeli war of 1967.
"The Israeli government, regrettably, does not have a strategy for peace ... The Israeli policy is aimed at burying the peace process by various means," al-Shara said.
Syria would accept nothing less than the full return of Golan territory, and he accused Israel's new right-wing government of reneging on previous commitments to trade land for peace.
"It is high time for Israel to realise that it will not be able to achieve peace and keep occupied territories," he said.
